summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was admitted after developing hypotension and chest pain during hemodialysis. She presented with altered mental status, which resolved, and was found to have leukocytosis. A urine culture identified Klebsiella pneumoniae, confirming a urinary tract infection. She received a single dose of intravenous vancomycin in the emergency department and was transitioned to oral antibiotics for home. Her hypotension improved after holding antihypertensive medications, and her condition stabilized. Warfarin was adjusted to increase INR to therapeutic levels. She was discharged home with services the following day in stable condition with instructions to continue dialysis, monitor weight, adhere to a low-sodium diet, and follow up with her primary care provider.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
